sections.title: Words for going online
sections.content: Going online has its own small set of words, and most are borrowed, so you will recognise them: *internet*, *e-mail* and *fájl* ("file"). Hungarian gives them the endings you already know: *az interneten* ("on the internet"), *e-mailt* ("an e-mail" as an object), *fájlt* ("a file" as an object). Two chunks you will use constantly: *Mi a wifi jelszó?* ("What is the wifi password?") and *Mi az e-mail címed?* ("What is your e-mail address?"). You know *wifi* from Unit 23, *jelszó* from Unit 43 and *cím* from A1. *e-mail cím* is written as two words.

items.english: Hi! What is the wifi password?

items.spanish: Nem működik az internet, hibás a wifi.
items.english: The internet isn't working, the wifi is faulty.
The file is in the e-mail.

sections.content: Foreign words take ordinary Hungarian endings: *e-mailt*, *e-mailben*, *fájlt*. Do not leave them bare after a verb like *küld*: say *Küldök egy e-mailt*, not *Küldök egy e-mail*.
